newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: Slovak SAX index up 3.42 pts on gains to Slovnaft.
newsitem.headline: Slovak SAX index up 3.42 pts on gains to Slovnaft.

text.p: Major Slovak shares closed higher in thin trading on the Bratislava Stock Exchange (BSE) on Monday, with gains to shares of refinery Slovnaft pushing the index up 3.42 points to 188.99.
Brokers said they expected the market to ease in near future, with shares appearing slightly over-valued.

"However, I think the market will then begin to rise again, moving in its obvious cycles," Dusan Sykora of ING Barings said. "It seems to be already normalising, after some uncertain developments since the new year."
He said steel maker VSZ, which closed up 20 crowns at 640,was the best example of normalising market.
"I expect VSZ will ease in the coming days and then rise again, hitting a normal cyclical share track," Sykora said.
Slovnaft, the most-heavily weighted issue on the index, gained 40 crowns to 850, while oil and gas storage firm Nafta rose 10 crowns at 1,710.
Overall volume fell to 441,392 shares, from 5,610,947 shares traded on Friday, while turnover decreased to 237.51 million crowns, from 909.34 million.
